methodology.note: Observed official catalog links are normalized into broad capability families for portfolio planning. Classification is deterministic keyword triage, not a claim of API equivalence; use the audit for the reviewed disposition.

getting-started.action: Publish a 15-30 line recipe and a separate incremental First Map walkthrough; keep the current qualified app as a project.

maps-camera-interaction.action: Document focused MapLibre camera, bounds, events, hit-test, and lifecycle recipes without inventing duplicate SDK wrappers.

data-sources-layers.action: Expose atomic recipes for GeoServices, OGC Features/Tiles, WFS, WMS/WMTS, OData, PMTiles, STAC, COG, GeoParquet, and file-backed GeoJSON; evaluate CSV/KML gaps separately.

query-filter.action: Add SQL, spatial, pagination, statistics, extent, selection, and cancellation recipes around the existing planner and protocol adapters.

visualization-styling.action: Productize a coherent renderer/style layer for categorical, class-break, continuous, heatmap, cluster, label, legend, and expression workflows; use MapLibre directly where that is the honest abstraction.

labels-popups.action: Add small label, popup, detail-panel, selection, and accessible feature-summary recipes; avoid forcing a proprietary popup model.

editing-drawing.action: Split sketch editing into create, update, delete, validation, form, conflict, and offline replay recipes plus one full field-operations project.

controls-ui.action: Publish one recipe per existing basemap switcher, layer list, legend, swipe, measurement, time slider, feature table, and editor component.

geocoding-search.action: Add forward, reverse, suggestions, local/custom source, and result-to-map walkthroughs; provide a stable quota-limited demo service or deterministic fixture.

routing-network.action: Ship route and directions first; treat service areas, optimization, map matching, and network analysis as explicit future capabilities rather than mock samples.

geometry-analysis.action: Publish projection, buffer, intersect, union, distance, area, and worker execution recipes; document unsupported operators explicitly.

analytics-widgets.action: Turn columnar, Deck.gl, Kepler, accessible table, and linked-state primitives into formula, categories, histogram, range, table, time-series, and spatial-filter recipes; add H3/Quadbin only with a real source contract.

raster-imagery.action: Build an imagery progression from WMS/WMTS to COG range reads, STAC search, imagery tiles, hillshade, terrain, and raster analytics using the Maui manifest.

time-realtime.action: Keep the incident dashboard as a project and add focused SSE, WebSocket, OData delta, checkpoint, reconciliation, and temporal playback recipes.

offline-sync.action: Make offline region, cache, quota, credential screening, edit queue, conflict resolution, and replay a flagship walkthrough and project.

authentication-security.action: Publish API key, bearer, OAuth/PKCE, client credentials, redaction, and browser-secret safety recipes with explicit deployment boundaries.

three-dimensional.action: Treat Cesium scene workspace as partial coverage; prioritize terrain, 3D buildings, camera sync, and time, while marking mesh, point cloud, voxel, BIM, viewshed, weather, and advanced scene analysis as gaps.

framework-integration.action: Keep core recipes framework-neutral; provide maintained Vite starters for React first, then Vue, Svelte, and Angular only when CI-owned.

portal-content.action: Build import, parse, save, share, and publish walkthroughs around web maps, saved workspaces, collaboration, and Studio; do not imply full ArcGIS Portal parity.

ai-agents.action: Decompose the AI projects into inspect-map, tool schema, plan, approval, execution receipt, and provider-adapter recipes, then retain full agent projects.

device-native.action: Route native device patterns to honua-mobile; retain only browser location, file, share, and permission patterns relevant to the Web SDK.

other.action: Review against product strategy before creating an example or SDK surface.
